game.title: Lathi Khela (Stick Fighting)
game.description: A traditional Bengali martial art form involving skilled stick fighting, historically used by lathials (warriors) employed by zamindars. Now performed during festivals and weddings as a cultural demonstration.
game.location: Rural areas, Kushtia, Jessore, villages throughout
game.occasion: Weddings, festivals, puja ceremonies, Eid celebrations
howToPlay: Step 1: Practitioners, known as lathials, train in basic stances and swings.
Step 2: Two opponents face each other holding long bamboo sticks.
Step 3: They perform choreographed routines demonstrating skill and agility.
Step 4: In competitive matches, fighters attempt to strike opponents while defending.
Step 5: Points are awarded for clean hits to permitted body areas.
Step 6: Fighters use spinning moves, jumps, and acrobatic defenses.
Step 7: Matches are accompanied by drumming and traditional music.
Step 8: Group performances show synchronized stick routines.
Step 9: The game emphasizes discipline, reflexes, and martial tradition.
Step 10: Annual conventions were historically held in Kushtia, now less frequent.
